trust_decision.summary: Whether an interpolated value is safe to paste into the Docker bundling `bash -c` script is decided only inside OsCommand.write/copy when the nodeModules file ops are rendered; both methods single-quote/interpolate their arguments without escaping them, so any dependency version or lock-file path is trusted verbatim.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Docker bundling' and 'NodejsFunction'; the first hit while reading the generated bundling command is the `echo '${data}' > "${filePath}"` rendering in OsCommand.write, which writeJson (bundling.ts:631-634) feeds with the JSON of the installed dependency versions.

fix_sites.entry_point: NodejsFunction with Docker bundling and nodeModules (function.ts:171 -> Bundling.bundle -> dockerFileOps -> writeJson -> write)
fix_sites.module_kind: internal helper class (OsCommand) in the aws-lambda-nodejs construct package

fix_sites.entry_point: NodejsFunction with Docker bundling and nodeModules; locks file copy, src derived from props.depsLockFilePath (bundling.ts:324, 333)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only interpolations the fix left unescaped (changeDirectory, remove/removeDir and the win32 branches of write/copy) are fed only by the fixed AssetStaging constants /asset-input and /asset-output, and the cmd.exe branch is dead because the Docker command is always rendered for osPlatform 'linux' (bundling.ts:236), so a solver can argue correctly that there is no attacker-influenced argument left to escape.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The win32/cmd.exe renderings of write and copy (`echo ^${data}^ > "..."`, `copy "src" "dest"`) are untouched by the fix, and the fixed-argument commands keep their double-quoted form (`cd "/asset-output"`, `rm -f "/asset-output/node_modules/.modules.yaml"`) which the existing tests assert verbatim; an over-broad fix that sends every OsCommand rendering through posixShellEscape rewrites those strings and breaks the suite.

O6_input_shapes: dependency version string containing a single quote, in the JSON body written by writeJson (fix.diff:66-92)
command-substitution payload `$(...)` in the lock-file path used as the src argument of copy (fix.diff:94-120)
JSON.stringify output that itself contains double quotes and must stay intact after escaping (bundling.ts:631-634)
empty data string for the pnpm-workspace.yaml write (bundling.ts:331)
both arguments of copy: variable src plus the constant package-manager lock-file name as dest (bundling.ts:641)

O7_producer.where: packages/aws-cdk-lib/aws-lambda-nodejs/lib/util.ts:135-151 (extractDependencies reads the project package.json via require() and falls back to the installed module's package.json; file: ranges are rewritten with a path join at util.ts:119-126)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new OsCommand file op (mkdir -p, chmod, touch, mv) rendered as `op "${arg}"` in the same style as changeDirectory.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: changeDirectory and remove/removeDir were left with the pre-fix unescaped double-quote idiom right next to the two fixed methods, so a maintainer adding another Docker file op would naturally copy that neighbour.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A cmd.exe rendering for a new file op (`mkdir "${dir}"`, `del "${file}"`) mirroring the untouched win32 branch of write/copy.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This fix deliberately fixed only the POSIX branch of write/copy, so any Windows counterpart added later starts from an unescaped template.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shell step spliced in as a pre-joined string (`this.packageManager.installCommand.join(' ')`), e.g. an install command extended with a registry or flag taken from props.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The docker file-ops step already mixes pre-joined raw strings with rendered OsCommand output, so a maintainer adding a configurable install flag would interpolate it into the same `&&` chain unescaped.

O9_family: OS command injection (shell metacharacter injection into a generated bash -c bundling script)
